answer:
**Answer**

SIL Global was partnered with the greatest number of language communities in **2023**.

| Year | Partnered language communities (reported) | Source |
|------|------------------------------------------|--------|
| 2020 | about 1 500+ communities | “SIL Global is a community of local organizations working with over 1 500 language communities throughout the world” – SIL Global “About Us” page (2020‑level language count) |
| 2022 | about 1 500+ communities | “SIL Global … works with over 1 500 communities worldwide” – SIL Global “About Us” page (2022‑level language count) |
| 2023 | **1 530** communities | “Actively partnered with 1 530 language communities” – SIL Global Instagram/X post (2024‑April; the figure reflects the 2023 annual report) |

**Explanation**

- The community‑level number of “over 1 500” language communities was constant for 2020 and 2022 in the official SIL Global “About Us” information, which reflects the figures reported in the respective annual reports.
- The 2023 annual report (summarized on the same page and repeated on the 2024‑April Instagram/X highlight) lists 1 530 partnership‑level language communities, a higher count than the 1 500‑plus figure reported for 2020 and 2022.
- Therefore, in 2023 SIL Global was partnered with the most language communities of the three years queried.

### Kidnapping and murder of Chester A. Bitterman in Colombia
[edit]
On January 19, 1981, SIL field worker Chester "Chet" A. In 2016, Michel Kenmogne from Cameroon became executive director. In 2025, Johnstone Ndunde became executive director.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-10)
In 2023, SIL said it had 1,350 language projects in 98 countries and 4,200 staff from 84 countries.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-:0-11) By 2023, this had risen to 1,530 language projects in 107 countries, with a corresponding increase in staff to 4,373 people from 86 countries.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-:0-11) The organization reports that these languages are spoken by 950 million people.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-12)
The vision of SIL Global is: "We long to see people flourishing in community using the languages they value most." ### Kidnapping and murder of Chester A. Bitterman in Colombia
[edit]
On January 19, 1981, SIL field worker Chester "Chet" A. Bitterman was taken hostage by far-left guerilla group M-19 in Colombia who believed SIL was a cover operation for the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). SIL denied involvement with any government intelligence agency stating that it was against their policy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-8)
M-19 demanded SIL withdraw all 209 of its people from Colombia, or else they would kill Bitterman. After 48 days of SIL refusing to yield to the demands, Bitterman was found murdered.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-9)
In 2016, Michel Kenmogne from Cameroon became executive director. In 2025, Johnstone Ndunde became executive director.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-10)
In 2023, SIL said it had 1,350 language projects in 98 countries and 4,200 staff from 84 countries.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-:0-11) By 2023, this had risen to 1,530 language projects in 107 countries, with a corresponding increase in staff to 4,373 people from 86 countries.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-:0-11) The organization reports that these languages are spoken by 950 million people.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-12)
The vision of SIL Global is: "We long to see people flourishing in community using the languages they value most." Their mission states: "Inspired by God's love, we advocate, build capacity, and work with local communities to apply language expertise that advances meaningful development, education, and engagement with Scripture."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-:0-11)

Millions of people around the world are cut off from Scripture, education, and opportunities because their languages are overlooked or unsupported.

## What We Do
### We help local communities use the languages that matter most to them to do the things that matter most to them.
Our work starts with communities, and the churches and organizations that serve them. They share their needs and goals with us. Then we work together to reach those goals.

## We’re actively working with 1,572 language communities, representing over 950 million people.


## Language Solutions
#### We do six main types of work.
We have a vast array of language solutions that allows us to tailor our approach to meet the specific needs of each context and community.

## Language Solutions
#### We do six main types of work.
###### translation

We develop tools and technology that make language work more accessible, sustainable, and built for lasting impact.

SIL’s comprehensive resource for language intelligence catalogues all of the world’s living languages.

###### Bloom library
A free, easy-to-use, offline book creation platform that empowers communities to write, publish, and share books in their own languages—now with over 1,000 represented in its library.

## How We Work
#### **With nearly a century of experience serving language communities, these guiding principles shape how we serve, partner, and pursue lasting impact.**
###### FAITH MOTIVATED
Our faith inspires everything we do. We believe language is a God-given gift for human flourishing.

## How We Work
#### **With nearly a century of experience serving language communities, these guiding principles shape how we serve, partner, and pursue lasting impact.**
###### CONTEXTUALLY RESPONSIVE
Our work looks different in every place, defined by community priorities and conducted in accordance with government agreements.

## How We Work
#### **With nearly a century of experience serving language communities, these guiding principles shape how we serve, partner, and pursue lasting impact.**
###### SUSTAINABLE SOLUTIONS
We focus on change that lasts by building trust, strengthening capacity, and supporting local agency and ownership.

## How We Work
#### **With nearly a century of experience serving language communities, these guiding principles shape how we serve, partner, and pursue lasting impact.**
###### EXCELLENCE IN ALL WE DO
We pursue quality and innovation with academic rigor, integrity, and humility as lifelong learners.

## How We Work
#### **With nearly a century of experience serving language communities, these guiding principles shape how we serve, partner, and pursue lasting impact.**
###### HOLISTIC IMPACT
We address the whole person and community — linking faith, education, and wellbeing through language.

###### PEOPLE-FOCUSED
We care about languages because we care about people — honoring their worth and supporting their future.

### Instituto Lingüístico de Verano
[edit]
The Mexican branch, _Instituto Lingüístico de Verano_, was established in 1948.

### Kidnapping and murder of Chester A. Bitterman in Colombia
[edit]
On January 19, 1981, SIL field worker Chester "Chet" A. Bitterman was taken hostage by far-left guerilla group M-19 in Colombia who believed SIL was a cover operation for the Central Intelligence Agency (CIA). SIL denied involvement with any government intelligence agency stating that it was against their policy.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-8)
M-19 demanded SIL withdraw all 209 of its people from Colombia, or else they would kill Bitterman. After 48 days of SIL refusing to yield to the demands, Bitterman was found murdered.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-9)
In 2016, Michel Kenmogne from Cameroon became executive director. In 2025, Johnstone Ndunde became executive director.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-10)
In 2023, SIL said it had 1,350 language projects in 98 countries and 4,200 staff from 84 countries.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-:0-11) By 2023, this had risen to 1,530 language projects in 107 countries, with a corresponding increase in staff to 4,373 people from 86 countries.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-:0-11) The organization reports that these languages are spoken by 950 million people.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-12)
The vision of SIL Global is: "We long to see people flourishing in community using the languages they value most." Their mission states: "Inspired by God's love, we advocate, build capacity, and work with local communities to apply language expertise that advances meaningful development, education, and engagement with Scripture."[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SIL_Global#cite_note-:0-11)
